mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here with me. Have you ever felt the way loss can echo through families, towns, even generations? In the American South, especially in places where family, community, and history are tightly woven, every story holds a little bit of that ache. That's exactly what we’re about to explore together through Jesmyn Ward’s remarkable memoir, Men We Reaped. Picture rural Mississippi: a place where hope and hardship live side by side, and where the struggles of poverty, racism, and limited opportunity shape the lives of so many young Black men. In this memoir, Ward takes us close—right into the heart of her own losses, tracing the stories of five men she loved deeply, including her brother. Their lives, their joys and heartbreaks, are intertwined with her own journey to adulthood, revealing just how connected we all are, and how the pain of losing someone isn’t just one person’s burden—it’s something that can ripple through whole communities. As Ward moves between past and present, she invites us to witness not just her grief, but the strength it takes to keep going, to remember, and to honor those who are gone. What if holding on to those memories, and even asking hard questions about survival and hope, was itself a powerful act of love and resistance? That’s what we’ll be uncovering here—how people find resilience in the face of repeated tragedy, and what it truly means to remember, together. So, let’s begin this journey side by side, ready to listen, reflect, and maybe find a little hope in the stories of Men We Reaped by Jesmyn Ward.
